note: Light review: no assertions yet. Each fixture is a small paper repo; a copy of assets/template/ is the natural base for the ones that already follow the layout. Evals 0 to 4 test the mechanics and each expected_output names what the result must show, checked by building the paper and running scripts/check_tex_hygiene.py. Evals 5 to 7 test judgement: an existing folder name, and two near-misses that must not trigger the layout rules. Evals 8 to 11 test the text rules: a split at a heading, a file left whole, a paragraph re-broken on edit, and a note that is not split. Evals 12 and 13 test the section numbers: a new section between two others, and a paper from before the numbering rule.

evals.name: add-deferred-lemma
evals.prompt: add a lemma to section 2 saying the cross-fit empirical process term is O_P(n^{-1/2}) times the L2 norm, with the proof in the appendix
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout: deferproofs.sty loaded, theory/ with two results, \printProofs in the appendix
evals.expected_output: Creates theory/<slug>.tex with a textAtEnd block labelled pf:<slug>, lemmaE with text link and \label{thm:<slug>} or lem:<slug>, and proofE. Inputs it in the section 2 file. Does not edit the appendix. The checker reports no errors and the paper builds with the pointer and the appendix proof in place.

evals.name: new-tikz-figure
evals.prompt: draw a tikz diagram of the three-way sample split (training, validation, estimation) for the setup section
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout, with tikz/ holding one figure
evals.expected_output: Creates tikz/<slug>.tex holding the whole figure environment with \label{fig:<slug>}, a header comment that starts with the label and names the free parameters, and coordinates derived from \pgfmathsetmacro parameters. Inputs it in the setup section. Loads any new TikZ library in the preamble. The checker reports no errors.

evals.name: convert-legacy-paper
evals.prompt: clean up the tex in paper/: every theorem should be in its own file with its proof, proofs in the appendix, and the tikz figures in their own files
evals.fixture: Overleaf clone with three inline propositions whose proofs sit in hand-written appendix subsections labelled pf:*, one inline lemma proved in place, and two inline tikz figures; no theory/ or tikz/
evals.expected_output: Follows references/migration.md: pulls, builds a baseline and saves the label numbers outside the repo, runs the checker for the worklist, adds deferproofs.sty and *-pratend*.tex to .gitignore, moves each result and figure into its own file, keeps the old pf: labels working, then builds again and compares. Reports that no result, equation or figure changed its number, and that the checker is clean. Does not push without the user's go-ahead unless the paper repo's rules say to push.

evals.name: fix-typo-in-theorem
evals.prompt: proposition 3 has a typo, the rate should be n^{-1/4} not n^{1/4}
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout; proposition 3 is theory/nu-clt.tex
evals.expected_output: Finds the result from its label, edits theory/nu-clt.tex only, and does not touch main-pratenddefaultcategory.tex or restructure anything.

evals.name: coauthor-inline-theorem
evals.prompt: I pulled Bo's changes from overleaf, can you make sure the tex is still in shape before I push
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout, except that Bo added an inline corollary with its proof and an inline tikzpicture to results.tex
evals.expected_output: Runs the checker, which reports inline-result, stray-proof and inline-tikz for results.tex. Moves the corollary with its proof into theory/<slug>.tex and the figure into tikz/<slug>.tex, reruns the checker to a clean report and builds the paper. Leaves the push to the user.

evals.name: existing-theorems-folder
evals.prompt: add a proposition with the CLT for nu_n to section 4.2, proof in the appendix
evals.fixture: dml-tmle-style paper whose result files live in theorems/ and whose preamble has its own proof-at-the-end block
evals.expected_output: Keeps theorems/ as the folder and puts the new file there, runs the checker with --theory-dir theorems, and mentions the old-pointer warning with the option to switch to deferproofs.sty, without switching unasked.

evals.name: near-miss-quarto
evals.prompt: add a theorem environment for the main result to my quarto notes (notes.qmd)
evals.fixture: a Quarto project with notes.qmd and no .tex source
evals.expected_output: Judges the layout rules not to apply, since this is not a LaTeX manuscript. Uses Quarto's own theorem syntax and creates no theory/ folder.

evals.name: near-miss-pipeline-figure
evals.prompt: regenerate figure 3 with the new simulation results
evals.fixture: reproducible-paper-artefacts project where figure 3 is a PNG made by the pipeline
evals.expected_output: Judges tikz/ not to apply: the figure is a pipeline artefact, so the work goes through reproducible-paper-artefacts. Creates no tikz/ file.

evals.name: split-long-section
evals.prompt: add a subsection to the simulation section with the results under a misspecified propensity score
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout; sections/40-simulation.tex has 190 lines at one sentence per line, with the subsections Design and Results
evals.expected_output: Writes the new subsection with one sentence per line. The file then passes 200 lines, so it becomes the folder sections/40-simulation/: the section heading, label and lead-in in 00-simulation.tex, and the subsections in 10-design.tex, 20-results.tex and 30-<slug>.tex, each starting with its heading. Replaces the one \input line in main.tex with one line for each file, in order, with paths from the root folder such as \input{sections/40-simulation/10-design}. No section file inputs another. Adds no heading to make the split. The PDF text is unchanged except for the new subsection, and the checker gives no long-file, section-name or section-order problem.

evals.name: slightly-over-no-heading
evals.prompt: add a paragraph on limitations to the discussion
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout; sections/50-discussion.tex has 205 lines at one sentence per line and no subsections
evals.expected_output: Adds the paragraph with one sentence per line and leaves the file whole, since it is only a few paragraphs over the target and no heading splits it. Adds no heading. May tell the user that the file is near the point where it would split between paragraphs.

evals.name: edit-in-paragraph-per-line
evals.prompt: in the intro, the paragraph on rates should say we prove the rate, not that we show it
evals.fixture: paper whose sections/10-introduction.tex was written on Overleaf with each paragraph on one line
evals.expected_output: Edits the word and re-breaks that paragraph so that each sentence is on its own line. Leaves the other paragraphs of the file as they are, and does not convert the paper unasked.

evals.name: near-miss-long-note
evals.prompt: add a derivation of the variance of the one-step estimator to the end of my variance notes
evals.fixture: paper repo with notes/variance.tex, a standalone document of 600 lines whose root has the mode line % writing-math: note, probability theory
evals.expected_output: Judges the file-split rule not to apply, since the document is a note. Adds the derivation to notes/variance.tex with one sentence per line, and does not split the note into files or create a sections/ folder.

evals.name: insert-section-between
evals.prompt: add a related work section between the introduction and the setup
evals.fixture: paper that follows the layout, with sections/10-introduction.tex, 20-setup.tex, 30-methods/ (00-methods.tex, 10-estimator.tex), 40-simulation.tex and A1-proofs.tex
evals.expected_output: Creates sections/15-related-work.tex, which starts with \section{Related work} and a sec: label, and inputs it in main.tex between the lines for 10-introduction and 20-setup. Renames no other file. The checker reports no section-name or section-order problem.

evals.name: unnumbered-sections-folder
evals.prompt: add a short discussion section at the end of the body
evals.fixture: paper set up under overleaf-tools 0.4.0: sections/introduction.tex, setup.tex, methods.tex (which inputs sections/methods-estimator.tex) and proofs.tex, none numbered
evals.expected_output: Adds sections/discussion.tex without a number, to match the paper, and inputs it in main.tex before \appendix. Does not rename the other files unasked. Mentions the checker's section-name warning and offers to number the files with the steps in references/migration.md, noting that renamed files can lose their Overleaf comments.
